Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
Current presentation: 27-year-old male, minutes after presumed wasp/bee sting to right arm, with local erythema and subjective lip tingling/mild dyspnoea. Examination shows localized reaction only; no objective airway compromise.

Consistent differential considerations:  
1. Localized allergic reaction to insect sting – most likely (high).  
2. Early IgE-mediated anaphylaxis – possible but currently no systemic signs (medium).  
3. Anxiety/panic response – contributing factor (medium).  

Plan discussed:  
• Start oral antihistamine (e.g., chlorphenamine 4 mg, up to six times daily, or once-daily non-sedating alternative) – dose/route/frequency beyond given example not documented.  
• Education on red-flag symptoms of anaphylaxis (lip/tongue swelling, stridor, worsening breathlessness, spreading rash, hypotension).  
• If symptoms progress, attend Emergency Department immediately; if concerned but stable, contact GP.  
• Monitor sting site; if erythema spreads, becomes hot, or systemic infection signs develop, seek review for possible antibiotics.  
• No immediate need for allergy testing; may reconsider if recurrent reactions.  
• Information link on anaphylaxis to be provided.

Management Plan
- Over-the-counter antihistamine as above.  
- Safety-net advice: call emergency services or attend A&E if airway compromise or systemic reaction develops.  
- GP follow-up if local symptoms worsen or recurrent reactions occur.  
- Patient provided reassurance and written information about anaphylaxis.

Consider:
- Pathology tests as above: consider only if recurrent reactions (not currently indicated)  
- EPC referral for allied health (10x visits/year): not recorded  
- Dental referral: not recorded  
- Optometry referral: not recorded  
- Audiometry referral: not recorded  
- Dietitian referral: not recorded  
- CTG registration (if not enrolled): not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Localized allergic reaction to insect sting – High likelihood: supported by isolated erythema and absence of systemic findings.  
- Early systemic allergic reaction/anaphylaxis – Moderate likelihood: rapid onset and lip/tongue sensations warrant caution despite normal exam.  
- Anxiety/panic attack – Moderate likelihood: subjective dyspnoea disproportionate to objective findings; history of anxiety.
